explanation: The SRY gene stands for the Sex determining Region of the Y chromosome. When this gene was experimentally injected into a single-cell mouse embryo, it caused all the resulting mice to develop as males. In genetic research, scientists can also perform gene knockouts, creating knockout mice. In these knockout mice, specific alleles are completely removed or rendered nonfunctional, allowing researchers to study the consequences of losing gene function.

questions.q: What does the SRY gene stand for, and what was the result of injecting it into a single-cell mouse embryo?
opts: Somatic Replication Yeast gene; it halted all embryo division.
Sex determining Region of Y chromosome; it caused all the mice to develop as males.
Systemic Regulatory Y-linkage; it generated larger mouse strains.
Starch Synthesis Regulator; it made the mice resistant to toxins.
